subject: Clarify: tenant-scoped carveout for ephemeral debug traces + evidence needed
messages:
From: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@novaforge.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security-team@novaforge.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Data retention question — tenant-scoped ephemeral debug traces

Marcus / Neha,

Thanks for taking this on — our SOC2 audit shop flagged a question around short-lived debug/tracing logs that are scoped per-tenant. Specifically: does Redwood support a tenant-level carveout that keeps debug traces for 90 days for a given customer while the default platform TTL is 30 days?

We need two things for our evidence package: a) a short write-up of the execution path that enforces tenant-scoped retention (who may trigger it, what controls prevent cross-tenant leakage), and b) artifacts to demonstrate the retention behavior (retention matrix, sample deletion job logs, or KMS key usage showing segregation).

I attached our intake form (Novaforge_DataRequestForm.pdf) and the SIG checklist references. Can you confirm what you can provide and an ETA? If a carveout is possible, we also need a short description of compensating controls (role separation, access logs, alerting) that auditors can read.

Appreciate a quick reply, we have a cutoff for evidence bundle on Tuesday.

— Alex
Alex Cheng
Head of Security Engineering, Novaforge
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@novaforge.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data retention question — tenant-scoped ephemeral debug traces

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. We're able to draft the required artifacts but need to coordinate a couple internal items so the deliverables are audit-ready.

High level answer up front: yes, Redwood can support tenant-specific retention carveouts for ephemeral debug traces via a tenant policy layer that controls retention windows plus RBAC and audit logging. We will provide a short architecture write-up, a retention_matrix export, and an export of deletion-run metadata that demonstrates the lifecycle for a test tenant.

Neha — can you pull the retention_matrix.csv for the default + sample carveout and include the deletion-run evidence (log snippets) and a short note on compensating controls (KMS, restricted dev access, alerting). Jordan — once we have that, please stage the artifacts in the shared drive link and we will produce a one-page summary for Novaforge.

Alex — ETA: EOD Monday if Neha can assemble the artifacts; otherwise mid-Wed. Is that acceptable for your audit timeline?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Product Manager, Security + Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data retention question — tenant-scoped ephemeral debug traces

Looping in a short summary here and attaching the artifacts we can deliver. Attachments: retention_matrix.csv (exported mapping of TTLs by log class / tenant flag) and a short deletion-run excerpt showing the job id and timestamp for a simulated tenant carveout run.

Quick notes (to use in the one-pager):
- Implementation: retention is enforced by the tenant policy controller at write-time and by a periodic deletion worker that reads TTL from the retention table; tenant-scoped carveouts are a flag on the tenant config and only accepted by a delegated admin role via the Admin API (RBAC).
- Compensating controls: KMS key per-tenant for sensitive debug payloads (optional), admin role separation (product ops vs infra), detailed audit logs (immutable append-only stream with sequence numbers), and scheduled alerts for deletion-job failures.
- Evidence provided: retention_matrix.csv, deletion_job_snippet.log (redacted), and a configuration snapshot showing the tenant flag set for a test tenant.

Caveats: For high-volume tenants we recommend a TTL carveout of no more than 90 days for debug traces — anything longer substantially increases storage and forensic exposure. Also note that encrypted ephemeral caches (KV) are not covered by the same TTL pipeline; if Novaforge needs those included we will need a follow-up technical change.

I staged the files here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-novaforge-evidence

Marcus / Jordan, I can produce the one-page summary and an auditor-friendly step-by-step on request.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Compliance & Controls Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@novaforge.com>

Thanks Neha — this is exactly what we needed.

I attached our SIG pack (Novaforge_SIG_Pack_v1.docx) with the auditor checklist — we'll drop the retention_matrix and deletion_job_snippet into the evidence bundle. Two quick follow-ups: 1) can you confirm the exact deletion_job run ids and times so we can reference them in the SIG table, and 2) can you send the one-page summary as a PDF for the bundle?

We have an auditor call Tuesday morning; a PDF by EOD Monday would be ideal. If needed we can take 30 minutes tomorrow to review.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

— Alex
Alex Cheng
Head of Security Engineering, Novaforge
